topic: Closed-margin sharp compatibility fibers for selection-PAG interventions. Given a finite COPAG, a positive rational selected law q, a bounded outcome h, and delta>0, characterize all SCMs whose selected MAG lies in the COPAG, P(V=v,S=1)=rho q(v), rho in [delta,1], and P(S=1|do(B=b))>=delta. Prove a graph-legal finite response representation, compactness and attained algebraic extrema, give elementary complexity bounds, and develop confidence-fiber inference. Use the binary saturated B circle-A witness with q=(1,2,3,4)/10, delta=1/4 and sharp interval [1/20,39/40]; Lee et al.'s survivor-selected cardiac-surgery FCI/LV-IDA analysis is the consumer. Distinguish Evans canonicalization, Rosset-Gisin-Wolfe cardinality, Duarte finite disturbance models, Yang PAG models, and Carey selected-marginalized graphs. PRESOLVE EVIDENCE REQUIRING VERIFICATION: For the saturated finite COPAG, presolve derives the exact interval [h_min+delta sum_{B=b}q(h-h_min), h_max-delta sum_{B=b}q(h_max-h)] with one-source attained endpoints and finite-sample coverage. Source merging by child set gives H<=2^N-1, and fixed-slot moment preservation gives K<=m+3; legality is retained when q is faithful. Exact arithmetic verifies the five-type witness and independent 32-response optimization. A positive XOR support-deletion example shows that moment preservation alone need not preserve actual edges, although an equal-moment legal lift exists. Checks included zero-width outcomes, vacuous interventions, delta endpoints, latent-child-set merging, shared normalization, graph deletion, and nearby canonicalization results without finding a full collision. UNRESOLVED BOTTLENECK: Prove compact exact-graph canonicalization and graph-legal lifting of limiting moments for every positive, potentially unfaithful q. EARLY KILL TEST: Settle the lifting lemma on a binary three-observed-variable COPAG with a compelled collider using essential-parent polynomial strata; an unattained closure endpoint with no legal lift kills the general theorem. STRONGEST-FORM DRAFT (unverified, gaps listed inside): <repo-root>/internal/presolve_drafts/scm_selpag_delta_closed_fiber.md.

open_problems.open_problem: Characterize the sharp range of a bounded population intervention mean over all finite SCMs represented by a selection COPAG that reproduce a positive selected law and satisfy a uniform lower bound on intervention-specific selection probability.

source_refs.claim: sIDP is sound and complete for point identification from ancestral graphs under selection bias, but failed identification returns no sharp identified set.
source_refs.author: Leihao Chen and Joris M. Mooij

source_refs.claim: P-NCM optimization supports counterfactual partial identification over observational PAGs but does not establish closed-margin exact-graph fibers under selection.
source_refs.author: Hongshuo Yang, Adiba Ejaz, Yushu Pan, and Elias Bareinboim

source_refs.claim: Discrete causal bounding for a fixed graph reduces to polynomial programming and can accommodate selection, but the graph is supplied rather than ranging over a selection-PAG class.
source_refs.author: Guilherme Duarte, Noam Finkelstein, Dean Knox, Jonathan Mummolo, and Ilya Shpitser
source_refs.venue: Journal of the American Statistical Association

source_refs.claim: A complete calculus identifies conditional effects common to a PAG class but does not characterize sharp bounds when identification fails.
source_refs.author: Amin Jaber, Adèle H. Ribeiro, Jiji Zhang, and Elias Bareinboim

open_problems.why_unsolved: The closest results divide the problem three ways: Chen and Mooij decide point identification under selection, Yang et al. optimize over categorical PAG-constrained models without an exact-graph closedness guarantee, and Duarte et al. compute sharp bounds for a fixed discrete DAG. None proves that the union over selection-compatible MAG and SCM realizations equals one finite algebraic fiber, remains closed when graph-essentiality conditions are imposed, or attains its extrema under only an intervention-specific lower selection margin.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A sharp identified-set formula or finite polynomial optimization characterization for the intervention mean, with a proof that its feasible set equals the original SCM class and that both endpoint values are attained.

writing_exemplar.why: Its motivation moves directly from PAG-induced structural uncertainty to optimization-based counterfactual partial identification.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: A learned PAG leaves many causal structures -> point-identification algorithms may fail -> optimization over compatible SCMs yields bounds -> selection margins require a closed, sharp compatibility fiber

method_exemplars.technique: Replace discrete structural equations by finitely many response types, translate observational and causal restrictions into polynomial constraints, and prove equivalence between the program and the original SCM problem.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The target is likewise a sharp discrete-SCM bound, but must couple multiple graph realizations and intervention-specific selection margins while preserving exact graph legality.

method_exemplars.technique: Use input-augmented ancestral graphs and selection-aware bucket and pc-component decompositions to isolate point-identified components.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The decomposition can remove identified components before unresolved components enter a sharp algebraic bounding program.

method_exemplars.technique: Construct width-adaptive confidence intervals from estimated bound endpoints and prove uniform coverage as the identification interval approaches a singleton.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Once the COPAG fiber yields attained scalar endpoints, the same endpoint-centered logic supplies inference that remains valid near point identification.

open_problems.open_problem: Determine whether every limiting feasible moment point of a positive selected-law COPAG fiber has a finite SCM lift preserving every required edge and inducing path, or exhibit a compelled-feature COPAG with an unattained exact-graph endpoint.

source_refs.claim: P-NCMs parameterize categorical SCMs represented by a PAG using continuous edge masks, whose zero-valued boundaries can change graph structure.
source_refs.author: Hongshuo Yang, Adiba Ejaz, Yushu Pan, and Elias Bareinboim

source_refs.claim: Canonical DAGs preserve latent-variable marginal and observed-intervention models without proving preservation of an exact selected-MAG stratum at parameter-space limits.
source_refs.author: Robin J. Evans

source_refs.claim: Faithful Bayesian networks form a dense open set, showing that exact-faithfulness or essential-edge strata are not automatically closed under limits.
source_refs.author: Philip Boeken, Patrick Forré, and Joris M. Mooij

source_refs.claim: Selected-marginalized directed graphs characterize interventional indistinguishability under latent confounding and selection but not compact exact-graph response-function realizations.
source_refs.author: Ryan Carey, Marina Maciel Ansanelli, Elie Wolfe, and Robin J. Evans

source_refs.excerpt: Construct equal observed behavior laws with finite hidden refinements having opposite overlap status

open_problems.why_unsolved: Evans-style canonicalization preserves observable distribution and intervention models, whereas the desired fiber must also retain graph-essential parents and inducing paths. Yang et al.'s masks and the openness result of Boeken, Forré, and Mooij expose the boundary problem: nonzero structural witnesses may vanish along a convergent sequence. The prior proposal supplies a finite latent-refinement strategy for preserving an observed experiment while changing a latent property, but its first proof step must be replaced by a response-function refinement that simultaneously preserves the selected law, intervention-selection margin, and exact selected-MAG stratum.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A necessary-and-sufficient polynomial-stratum lifting characterization for limiting selected-law and interventional-moment vectors, yielding either a compact exact-graph realization theorem or an explicit positive finite counterexample with an unattained boundary point.

writing_exemplar.why: It frames the problem as representing all SCMs behind a PAG without enumerating the equivalence class and separates structural representation from downstream optimization.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Observational data determine only a PAG -> conclusions must range over compatible SCMs -> continuous masks encode structural uncertainty -> exact selected-graph fibers require control of mask-boundary graph deletion

method_exemplars.technique: Canonicalize hidden-variable DAGs by latent projection, exogenizing latent variables and merging redundant latent child sets, with proof by equality of marginal and intervention models.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The desired lift begins with the same canonicalization but must strengthen distributional equivalence to preservation of selected-MAG graphical features.

method_exemplars.technique: Analyze faithfulness in total-variation topology and perturb Markov kernels while controlling conditional-independence constraints.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Its topology isolates why an exact-graph stratum can lose edges at a limit and identifies the obstruction a legal lifting lemma must overcome.

method_exemplars.technique: Canonicalize DAGs with marginalized and selected vertices into smDGs and prove equivalence through interventional indistinguishability.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The smDG construction is the closest selection-aware quotient, but the resolution must refine experiment equivalence into exact finite realizability at fiber boundaries.

open_problems.open_problem: Find constructive uniform bounds on the numbers and cardinalities of latent child-set sources and response-function types needed to realize every feasible finite selection-COPAG compatibility fiber without deleting required graphical features.

source_refs.claim: Finite latent-cardinality bounds make finite-input and finite-output network-correlation sets closed, connected, and semialgebraic.
source_refs.author: Denis Rosset, Nicolas Gisin, and Elie Wolfe

source_refs.claim: Carathéodory reductions yield finite disturbance models and response types for discrete causal bounding on a fixed canonical DAG.
source_refs.author: Guilherme Duarte, Noam Finkelstein, Dean Knox, Jonathan Mummolo, and Ilya Shpitser
source_refs.venue: Journal of the American Statistical Association

source_refs.claim: mDAG canonicalization replaces latent structure by exogenous sources indexed by relevant observed child sets while preserving marginal causal models.
source_refs.author: Robin J. Evans

source_refs.claim: The P-NCM construction may require exponentially many latent variables and identifies scalability and more efficient inducing-path constraints as open challenges.
source_refs.author: Hongshuo Yang, Adiba Ejaz, Yushu Pan, and Elias Bareinboim

source_refs.excerpt: The lower family uses O(log T) latent states and therefore says nothing about a uniformly bounded latent alphabet.

open_problems.why_unsolved: Rosset, Gisin, and Wolfe prove cardinality bounds for network-local hidden variables, Duarte et al. obtain finite disturbances after fixing a canonical DAG, and Evans reduces latent structure by child-set canonicalization. A selection COPAG adds a union of exact graphical strata, shared normalization through the selected law, and intervention-specific selection inequalities. The prior proposal highlights the general distinction between unrestricted and uniformly bounded latent alphabets, but transferring that distinction requires replacing its depth-state counting by child-set merging and fixed-slot moment compression. Ordinary Carathéodory compression preserves moments but can erase essential-parent or inducing-path witnesses.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A constructive graph-indexed cardinality-reduction theorem with explicit bounds in observed-state count and imposed moments, an elementary encoding-size bound, and either matching lower-bound examples or a proof that the reduction preserves every required essential parent and latent child set.

writing_exemplar.why: It motivates latent-cardinality bounds through the topological and algebraic properties they unlock.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Latent variables appear unbounded -> finite observed alphabets permit support compression -> explicit cardinality bounds yield closed semialgebraic compatibility sets -> selection-COPAG compression must additionally retain graph legality

method_exemplars.technique: Apply convex-geometric support reduction source by source while holding remaining latent sources fixed, then deduce compactness and semialgebraicity from the finite parameterization.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Selection-COPAG sources also have finite observed interfaces, but support reduction must additionally retain witnesses for required graphical features.

method_exemplars.technique: Encode deterministic response-function strata and use Carathéodory arguments to cap exogenous support while preserving factual and counterfactual moments.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The target concerns the same response-function simplex, augmented by graph-essentiality certificates.

method_exemplars.technique: Merge latent variables according to maximal observed child sets and prove that the canonical mDAG has the same marginal causal model.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Child-set merging is the natural first reduction before response-type support is compressed.

open_problems.open_problem: Develop confidence-fiber inference for sharp intervention bounds from a finite selection COPAG when the selected multinomial law and possibly the COPAG are estimated from the same clinical sample.

source_refs.claim: The cardiac-surgery analysis learns a PAG by FCI and applies LV-IDA to possible effects on postoperative length of stay, creating a need for uncertainty quantification over graph and effect ambiguity.
source_refs.author: Jaron J. R. Lee, Ranjani Srinivasan, Chin Siang Ong, Diane Alejo, Stefano Schena, Ilya Shpitser, Marc Sussman, Glenn J. R. Whitman, and Daniel Malinsky
source_refs.venue: Journal of Thoracic and Cardiovascular Surgery

source_refs.claim: Resampling and screening gives asymptotically valid causal-effect intervals after constraint-based discovery, principally for PC, Gaussian DAGs, and point-valued adjustment effects.
source_refs.author: Ting-Hsuan Chang, Zijian Guo, and Daniel Malinsky

source_refs.claim: Criterion inversion yields estimators and confidence regions for identified sets defined by moment equalities and inequalities.
source_refs.author: Victor Chernozhukov, Han Hong, and Elie Tamer

source_refs.claim: Uniformly valid confidence intervals for an interval-identified scalar require special handling as the interval width approaches zero.
source_refs.author: Guido W. Imbens and Charles F. Manski

open_problems.why_unsolved: Generic identified-set inference treats a fixed criterion, while post-discovery inference currently targets point effects mainly in Gaussian DAG or CPDAG settings. The desired object is a nonlinear semialgebraic image of a selected multinomial law, can change active algebraic faces or collapse to a singleton, and may be indexed by an FCI-derived graph with latent and selection variables. Lee et al.'s clinical workflow uses FCI followed by LV-IDA but does not provide coverage for a nonparametric selection-aware compatibility fiber.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A computable random confidence fiber or endpoint confidence intervals with finite-sample or uniform asymptotic coverage over positive laws satisfying the selection margin, Hausdorff consistency, and a graph-selection-aware coverage theorem when the COPAG is learned.

writing_exemplar.why: It supplies the clinical motivation, retrospective EHR regime, FCI-to-PAG workflow, and LV-IDA consumer language.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Cardiac-surgery EHR data contain latent confounding -> FCI represents structural ambiguity by a PAG -> LV-IDA reports possible causal effects -> a selection-aware confidence fiber is needed for calibrated intervention claims

method_exemplars.technique: Resample conditional-independence statistics, screen graph candidates, and union graph-specific confidence intervals while proving target coverage.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The same resampling-and-union architecture can propagate FCI and COPAG uncertainty, with graph-specific point-effect intervals replaced by confidence images of compatibility fibers.

method_exemplars.technique: Invert sample-criterion level sets encoding moment equalities and inequalities and establish set consistency, rates, and confidence-region validity.
method_exemplars.why_closest: A finite response representation turns the compatibility fiber into such a constrained criterion set, though singular faces and estimated graphs require new uniformity arguments.

method_exemplars.technique: Studentize estimated lower and upper endpoints with a critical value adapted to identification width and prove coverage through the point-identified boundary.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Sharp COPAG bounds can have zero or positive width depending on the selected law, so boundary-uniform inference is unavoidable.

open_problems.open_problem: Characterize sharp compatibility fibers when a selection COPAG is refined by finitely many observational, hard-intervention, or surrogate-intervention distributions that must share one latent response-function model.

source_refs.claim: The paper identifies extension from observational PAGs to equivalence classes refined by interventional distributions or other causal knowledge as future work.
source_refs.author: Hongshuo Yang, Adiba Ejaz, Yushu Pan, and Elias Bareinboim

source_refs.claim: smDG equality characterizes indistinguishability under observed-variable interventions but does not give a distribution-level sharp fiber for partially observed regimes.
source_refs.author: Ryan Carey, Marina Maciel Ansanelli, Elie Wolfe, and Robin J. Evans

source_refs.claim: Sigma-calculus gives sound identification procedures using observational and surrogate-experimental distributions for interventions on a specified causal structure.
source_refs.author: Juan D. Correa and Elias Bareinboim

source_refs.claim: Input-augmented PAGs unify observational and interventional regimes under selection for point identification, leaving sharp multi-regime partial identification untreated.
source_refs.author: Leihao Chen and Joris M. Mooij

open_problems.why_unsolved: Yang et al. explicitly leave intervention-refined equivalence classes open; Carey et al. answer a structural indistinguishability question rather than compatibility with specified regime laws; and Correa and Bareinboim and Chen and Mooij provide point-identification calculi. The first proof step that changes from a single selected-law fiber is the moment map: every regime must share response functions and latent-source probabilities, while regime-specific selection normalizations create coupled rational or homogenized polynomial constraints. The located literature supplies no sharp, attained finite-fiber characterization for this combination.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A sound and complete finite semialgebraic characterization of jointly compatible regime laws and resulting sharp intervention-query bounds, with an explicit shared-response representation and attained extrema.

writing_exemplar.why: It directly motivates moving from observational PAG uncertainty to equivalence classes refined by interventional evidence.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Observational PAGs encode a large SCM class -> compatible-model optimization yields counterfactual bounds -> experiments refine structural and distributional uncertainty -> a shared multi-regime selection-aware fiber is required

method_exemplars.technique: Represent hard, conditional, and stochastic intervention regimes in a unified calculus and recursively combine observational and surrogate-experimental distributions.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Its regime bookkeeping supplies the graphical side of the joint fiber, while the new result must retain rather than eliminate nonidentified components.

method_exemplars.technique: Construct one response-function polynomial program whose variables encode shared counterfactual behavior across factual and interventional quantities.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Sharing response types across regimes prevents separate optimizations from producing bounds incompatible with any single SCM.

method_exemplars.technique: Invert a sample criterion containing multiple moment equalities and inequalities to obtain confidence regions for a joint identified set.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The multi-regime fiber is estimated from coupled empirical moment vectors, making criterion inversion the closest established inference route.

literature_map:
Richardson and Spirtes (2002, Annals of Statistics) establish MAGs as representations of latent confounding and selection through ancestral-graph Markov models.
Zhang (2008, JMLR) develops causal reasoning with ancestral graphs and the PAG language used by FCI-based effect analysis.
Jaber, Ribeiro, Zhang, and Bareinboim (2022, NeurIPS) give complete conditional-effect identification over PAG classes but not sharp bounds after identification failure.
Chen and Mooij (2026, arXiv:2603.26301) extend completeness to ancestral graphs with selection and inputs through sIDP and iCOPAGs; the result is point identification rather than compatibility-fiber geometry.
Yang, Ejaz, Pan, and Bareinboim (2026, CausalAI R-153) directly parameterize categorical SCMs behind a PAG and optimize counterfactual bounds while flagging exponential latent structure and intervention-refined PAGs as open.
Carey, Ansanelli, Wolfe, and Evans (2025, arXiv:2509.20433) introduce selected-marginalized directed graphs and characterize structural indistinguishability under latent confounding, selection, and observed interventions.
Chen, Zoeter, and Mooij (2024, arXiv:2401.06925) define SCM conditioning for latent selection and prove compatibility with marginalization and intervention without deriving finite sharp fibers.
Evans (2016, Scandinavian Journal of Statistics) canonicalizes hidden-variable DAG margins into mDAGs and preserves observed-variable interventions; exact graph-stratum closure is outside that theorem.
Rosset, Gisin, and Wolfe (2018, Quantum Information and Computation) derive latent-cardinality bounds and closed semialgebraic correlation sets for finite causal networks.
Wolfe, Spekkens, and Fritz (2019, Journal of Causal Inference) develop inflation as a causal-compatibility hierarchy, emphasizing that compatibility is stronger than conditional-independence checking.
Duarte, Finkelstein, Knox, Mummolo, and Shpitser (2024, JASA) turn fixed-graph discrete causal bounds, including selection problems, into sharp polynomial programs with finite disturbances.
Boeken, Forré, and Mooij (2026 version, arXiv:2410.16004) prove faithful Bayesian networks are dense and open, exposing the closure tension for exact-edge compatibility fibers.
Lee et al. (2023, Journal of Thoracic and Cardiovascular Surgery) provide the consumer application: FCI learns a cardiac-surgery PAG and LV-IDA estimates possible effects on postoperative length of stay.
Malinsky and Spirtes (2017, PGM) develop LV-IDA effect bounds for linear-Gaussian ancestral-graph models without the nonparametric selected-law fiber considered here.
Chernozhukov, Hong, and Tamer (2007), Imbens and Manski (2004), and Chang, Guo, and Malinsky (2026) supply complementary identified-set, endpoint, and post-discovery inference machinery, but none covers a learned selection-PAG semialgebraic confidence fiber.
